mainTopic: Laws of פסולי המוקדשין whose הקדש came before their מום: their offspring, slaughter outside, and why their post-פדיון תמורה must die
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: the ברייתא's general rule (כלל) adds the milk of redeemed פסולי המוקדשין to the prohibition. The גמרא then reads the ברייתא closely. From its wording it infers that blemished offspring can be redeemed, which seems to refute רב הונא. רב הונא answers that the wording only copies the רישא for parallel style (אַיְּידֵי). Next, רב הונא reads 'חייב' instead of 'פטור' for slaughtering these animals outside. He sets the case as a minor eye blemish, following רבי עקיבא. The ברייתא then says such an animal makes a תמורה even after its פדיון. רבה בר אבוה rules that this תמורה must die, because it can be neither offered nor redeemed. רב עמרם asks why it is not simply eaten with its blemish, like the תמורה of a בכור or מעשר. אביי answers that every תמורה follows the animal it replaced. A ברייתא then finds a source in the פסוק 'ממעלי הגרה... טמא', which leads to a back-and-forth about the five חטאות מתות and תמורת אשם. Finally, a new משנה begins about a Jew who takes animals from a gentile as צאן ברזל; it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The extra word includes the animal's milk
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of an earlier discussion: the ברייתא's general rule (כלל) comes to include the milk (חלב) of redeemed פסולי המוקדשין in the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: This word comes to include its milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier point. It explains that the ברייתא's general rule (כלל) teaches that the milk of a redeemed blemished קדשים animal is also forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the ברייתא said that the milk of such animals is forbidden. The גמרא asked what the ברייתא's general rule (כללו של דבר) comes to add. The answer here is that it includes the milk in the prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: To include / to bring in (something extra, here from a general rule)
Its milk
Consecrated animals that became disqualified through a blemish and were redeemed

steps.confusionAlert: Here חלב (with a קמץ under the ח) means MILK, not forbidden fat (חֵלֶב). The topic is whether you may drink the milk of a redeemed קדשים animal.

phrases.english: to include its milk.
phrases.notes: The conclusion of a derivation that began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a derivation that began on the previous amud.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word in the verse includes the milk in the prohibition.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא about the offspring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes a line from the ברייתא so it can analyze it: offspring are not redeemed while unblemished and are not dedicated for any offering one wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: They may not be redeemed while unblemished, and one may not dedicate them for any offering he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes one line about the offspring of animals whose הקדש came before their blemish. This sets up the inferences in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These offspring are fully holy. So, unlike the offspring in the רישא (where the blemish came first), they cannot be redeemed while unblemished. They also cannot be switched into any type of קרבן the owner chooses.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said' – a formula for re-quoting an earlier source in order to analyze it
Are redeemed (פדיון)
Unblemished animals
One dedicates them (assigns them the status of a particular offering)

phrases.english: The Master said: They may not be redeemed while unblemished,
and one may not dedicate them for any offering he wants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's text to analyze a new line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offspring of animals whose הקדש came before their blemish are not redeemed while unblemished and are not dedicated for any offering one wants.

steps.title: Two inferences from the wording
steps.stepSummary: From the specific words of the ברייתא, the גמרא infers that blemished offspring CAN be redeemed, and that the offspring CAN be dedicated for the same offering as its mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only unblemished ones that may not be redeemed, which implies that blemished ones may be redeemed. It is only 'for any offering he wants' that one may not dedicate them, which implies that for the same offering one may dedicate them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely and draws a דיוק (inference) from each of its two phrases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'unblemished' implies a contrast: blemished offspring may be redeemed. The phrase 'any offering he wants' also implies a contrast: dedicating the offspring for the SAME offering as the mother is allowed. Both inferences come from reading a limit into the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Are redeemed (Aramaic for נפדין)
'But' / 'this implies' – introduces the opposite inference
Blemished animals
For that same offering (the mother's offering)

phrases.english: It is unblemished ones that are not redeemed,
which implies that blemished ones are redeemed.
It is for any offering he wants that one may not dedicate them,
which implies that for the same offering, one may dedicate them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּמִימִים הוּא דְּלָא מִיפַּרְקִי, הָא בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין מִיפַּרְקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws inferences from the quoted line.
steps.raayaObject: That blemished offspring can be redeemed and can be dedicated for the mother's offering.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The precise wording of the ברייתא ('unblemished', 'any offering he wants').

steps.title: What case fits both inferences?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a concrete case in which both inferences work together.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you find it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a real-life case that matches both inferences at once. The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two inferences need to be combined into one coherent scenario. That scenario will then be tested against רב הונא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find it? (asking for a concrete case)

phrases.english: How can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two inferences play out in a single case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete scenario matching both inferences.

steps.title: Dedicate for the same offering, redeem once blemished
steps.stepSummary: The case: one dedicates the offspring for the mother's offering, and if it later gets a blemish it is redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where one dedicates them for the same offering, and they are redeemed once they have a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The offspring is dedicated for the same type of offering as its mother, and if it becomes blemished it may be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This joins both inferences into one path. The offspring is used for the mother's קרבן, and if it develops a מום it can be redeemed. That leaves no room for 'letting it die.'

keyTerms.meaning: With their blemish (once they become blemished)

phrases.english: Where one dedicates them for the same offering,
and they are redeemed with their blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are dedicated for the mother's offering and are redeemed once blemished.

steps.title: Is this a refutation of רב הונא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that this reading of the ברייתא refutes רב הונא, who holds that such offspring are never redeemed and are left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב הונא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. According to the ברייתא's inference, blemished offspring may be redeemed, but רב הונא says they may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds that these offspring cannot be redeemed even with a blemish, so one leaves them to die. The inference from step 3 says the opposite. If that inference is correct, his view goes against a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a tentative suggestion)
A refutation from a tannaitic source
An אמורא who holds that these offspring are never redeemed

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav Huna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case from step 5 to attack רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that the offspring cannot be redeemed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's wording implies that blemished offspring are redeemed, which contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: The wording is only for symmetry
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that blemished offspring also cannot be redeemed. The סיפא only copied the wording of the רישא to keep the two clauses parallel, so no inference can be drawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can say to you: The same is true that even blemished ones are not redeemed. Since the first clause taught 'they are redeemed unblemished', the latter clause also taught 'they are not redeemed unblemished'. And since the first clause taught 'for any offering he wants', the latter clause also taught 'for any offering he wants'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא rejects the inferences. He says the words 'unblemished' and 'any offering he wants' in the סיפא are there only to mirror the רישא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא (blemish before הקדש), the words were meaningful: the offspring really are redeemed even while unblemished. The סיפא reused the same words just for style, using the 'אַיְּידֵי' principle. So no דיוק can be drawn from them, and blemished offspring are not redeemed either.

keyTerms.meaning: [He] can say to you – introduces a defense of a view
The same law applies
Since (it said X there, it also said X here) – wording copied for parallel style
The first clause / the latter clause

steps.whatToRemember: An inference from wording can be pushed aside by 'אַיְּידֵי': the words were written to match the parallel clause, not to teach a law. So רב הונא's view stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic tool across ש״ס for defending against a דיוק: not every word in a ברייתא or משנה carries legal weight.

phrases.english: Rav Huna can say to you:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין אֵין נִפְדִּין,
phrases.english: the same is true, that even blemished ones are not redeemed,
and since the first clause taught 'they are redeemed unblemished',
the latter clause also taught 'they are not redeemed unblemished',
and since the first clause taught 'for any offering he wants',
the latter clause also taught 'for any offering he wants'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב הונא against the refutation of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism (אַיְּידֵי): the wording carries no legal inference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'unblemished' and 'any offering' imply that blemished offspring are redeemed and that same-offering dedication is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those words only mirror the רישא. Blemished offspring are not redeemed either, so רב הונא stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inferences treat parallel stylistic wording as if it set a legal limit.

steps.title: Slaughtering these animals outside the Temple is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that one who slaughters these blemished קדשים (whose הקדש came before their מום) outside the עזרה is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next clause of the same ברייתא. That clause says that slaughtering these animals outside the Temple brings no punishment. This line sets up רב הונא's different reading, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment of כרת for שחוטי חוץ applies only to an animal that is fit to be brought on the מזבח. These animals have a מום, so they are not fit for the מזבח. That is why slaughtering them outside is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: One who slaughters a sacrifice outside the Temple courtyard (שחוטי חוץ)
Exempt from punishment
Outside the עזרה (Temple courtyard)

phrases.english: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the קדשים whose הקדש came before their blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the ברייתא that was being analyzed in steps 3 through 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering these blemished קדשים outside the עזרה carries no liability.

steps.title: רב הונא's version: liable, in a case of a minor eye blemish
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reads the ברייתא as 'חייב.' He sets the case as a minor blemish on the cornea of the eye, following רבי עקיבא, who says that if such animals went up on the מזבח, they are not taken down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא taught it as 'liable.' He sets the case as a blemish on the cornea of the eye, and according to רבי עקיבא, who says: if they went up on the altar, they are not taken down.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא has a different text of the ברייתא: 'liable' instead of 'exempt.' He explains how that reading can make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny blemish on the cornea of the eye is a weak מום. According to רבי עקיבא, an animal with such a blemish that was already put on the מזבח stays there and is offered. Since it is partly fit for the מזבח, slaughtering it outside makes a person חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches the text as (a different version of the wording)
He sets the case in (a specific situation)
Minor blemishes on the cornea of the eye
If they went up on the altar, they are not taken down

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is not saying every blemished animal makes you liable for slaughtering it outside. He means only a very minor eye blemish, and only according to רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Rav Huna taught it as 'liable,'
and he sets it in the case of minor blemishes on the cornea of the eye,
and according to Rabbi Akiva, who says:
if they went up on the altar, they are not taken down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the clause quoted in step 8, together with a case setting that fits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering outside is חייב when the blemish is a minor eye blemish, according to רבי עקיבא's view that such animals are offered if already on the מזבח.

steps.title: The animal makes a substitute both before and after redemption
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that these animals can make a תמורה whether before or after their פדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether before its redemption or after its redemption, it makes a substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the ברייתא. This sets up רב נחמן's ruling about what happens to that substitute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after פדיון, some of the original קדושה stays on the animal. Because of that leftover קדושה, trying to swap another animal for it still makes the new animal holy as a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption: transferring the animal's holiness onto money
Makes a substitute: an animal swapped for it becomes holy too

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנוֹ בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנוֹ
phrases.english: Whether before its redemption or after its redemption,
it makes a substitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנוֹ בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנוֹ עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קדשים animal whose הקדש came before its מום makes a תמורה even after its פדיון.

steps.title: A substitute made after redemption must die
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, rules that a תמורה made after the animal's פדיון is left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: and its substitute made after its redemption must die.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a ruling to the ברייתא's clause: a substitute made after redemption may not be used at all. It is left to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only told us that a תמורה takes effect. רבה בר אבוה (reported by רב נחמן) tells us what happens to that תמורה next. When it was made after the פדיון, it has no way out except dying.

keyTerms.meaning: It dies: it is locked away until it dies, with no use permitted
The אמורא whose ruling רב נחמן reports

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
And its substitute made after its redemption must die.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical ruling to the clause quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תמורה made after פדיון is left to die.

steps.title: Why must it die?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבה בר אבוה's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this substitute must die. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving a holy animal to die is the most extreme outcome. So the גמרא wants to know why no better option is available.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic behind the rule that a תמורה made after פדיון must die.

steps.title: It cannot be offered and cannot be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The תמורה cannot be offered, because it comes from a קדושה דחויה. It cannot be redeemed, because its holiness is too weak to pass onto money. So it must die.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should we do with it? Offer it? It comes from the power of rejected holiness. Redeem it? Its holiness is not strong enough to pass onto redemption money. Therefore it dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through each possible way to deal with the animal and rules each one out. Since nothing else works, the animal must die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offering it is ruled out, because its holiness came from an animal that was already pushed away from the מזבח (קדושה דחויה). Redeeming it is ruled out, because its holiness is too weak to 'grab onto' redemption money. With both options closed, the only result left is that it dies.

keyTerms.meaning: What should we do?
Rejected holiness: holiness that was pushed away from the מזבח
It is not strong enough
To pass its holiness onto its redemption money

steps.whatToRemember: A תמורה made after פדיון is stuck. It cannot be offered, because its holiness comes from a קדושה דחויה. It cannot be redeemed, because its holiness is too weak to pass onto money. So it is left to die.

phrases.english: What should we do with it?
Offer it? It comes from the power of rejected holiness;
Redeem it? It is not strong enough to pass its holiness onto its redemption money;
therefore it dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Offering is impossible because of קדושה דחויה, and redemption is impossible because the holiness is too weak, so death is the only option.

steps.title: רב עמרם: let the owners eat it with its blemish
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם objects: why not let the owners eat this תמורה once it has a מום, just as the תמורה of a בכור or מעשר is eaten?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם challenged it: But let it be eaten in its blemished state by the owners! What difference is there between this and the substitute of a firstborn or tithe animal?
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם challenges the ruling that the animal must die. He suggests a third option the גמרא did not mention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 claimed there was no way out besides death. רב עמרם points to a known case where a תמורה is simply eaten with its מום by the owners, with no פדיון needed. If that works there, why not here?

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it
Let it be eaten in its blemished state by the owners
What is the difference between

phrases.english: Rav Amram challenged it:
But let it be eaten in its blemished state by the owners!
And what is the difference between this
and the substitute of a firstborn or tithe animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 13 that death is the only option.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר אבוה's ruling that a תמורה made after פדיון must die.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a third option, eating it with its מום, just as with the תמורה of a בכור or מעשר.

steps.title: The source: a firstborn's or tithe's substitute is eaten with its blemish
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם cites a משנה: the תמורה of a בכור or מעשר, and its offspring for all generations, have the same law as a בכור or מעשר and are eaten with their מום by the owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: the substitute of a firstborn or tithe animal, they, their offspring, and the offspring of their offspring, until the end of the world, are like the firstborn and tithe, and they are eaten in their blemished state by the owners.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם backs up his challenge with a משנה (from מסכת תמורה). It shows that there is a case where a blemished תמורה is simply eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה proves that a תמורה can be eaten with its מום without any פדיון. That gives real force to רב עמרם's question of why our תמורה should be different.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Their offspring
Until the end of the world, meaning for all generations
Firstborn animal and animal tithe

phrases.english: As we learned: the substitute of a firstborn or tithe animal,
they, and their offspring, and the offspring of their offspring,
until the end of the world,
are like the firstborn and the tithe,
and they are eaten in their blemished state by the owners!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the comparison raised in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That a blemished תמורה can be eaten by the owners without פדיון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in תמורה: the תמורה of a בכור or מעשר is eaten with its מום by the owners.

steps.title: אביי: each substitute follows the law of its source animal
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that each תמורה carries the 'name' of the animal it replaced. בכור and מעשר are themselves eaten with a מום, so their תמורה is too. Our תמורה comes from an animal that needed פדיון, so it cannot be eaten that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: This one carries its mother's name, and that one carries its mother's name. This one is entirely called 'the substitute of a firstborn or tithe.' Just as a firstborn and tithe are eaten in their blemished state by the owners, so too their substitute is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבה בר אבוה. He shows that the case of בכור and מעשר is different from our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמורה follows the law of the animal it was swapped for (its 'mother'). A blemished בכור or מעשר is eaten by its owners without any פדיון, so its תמורה is eaten too. Our animal could only become permitted through פדיון, and its תמורה cannot be redeemed, so that path is closed and it still must die.

keyTerms.meaning: Its mother's name is on it: it follows the law of the animal it replaced
It is called
It is eaten

steps.whatToRemember: A תמורה always follows its source animal. A בכור or מעשר is eaten with its מום, so its תמורה is eaten. A redeemed קדשים animal needed פדיון, so its post-פדיון תמורה cannot be eaten and must die.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule: you decide the law of a תמורה by looking at the law of the animal it replaced.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
This one carries its mother's name,
and that one carries its mother's name.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה כּוּלּוֹ תְּמוּרַת בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר מִיקַּרְיָא,
phrases.english: This one is entirely called 'the substitute of a firstborn or tithe':

phrases.aramaic: מָה בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר בְּמוּמָן מִיתְאַכְלָן לַבְּעָלִים,
phrases.english: just as a firstborn and tithe are eaten in their blemished state by the owners,
so too their substitute is eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: זֶה שֵׁם אִמּוֹ עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עמרם's challenge in steps 14 and 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): each תמורה follows the law of its source animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every blemished תמורה can be eaten by its owners, just like the תמורה of a בכור or מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a תמורה whose source animal is itself eaten with a מום (בכור, מעשר) may be eaten. A תמורה made after פדיון still must die.

steps.title: Our תמורה needs פדיון but cannot get it
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his answer. Our תמורה carries the name of קדשים, and קדשים are eaten only after פדיון. Its holiness is too weak to pass onto money, so it can never be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this animal carries its mother's name: it is called 'the תמורה of קדשים'. Just as קדשים are eaten only through פדיון, so their תמורה is also eaten only through פדיון. But this one is not strong enough for its פדיון to take hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes אביי's answer to רב עמרם by applying the 'name' rule to our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בכור and מעשר can be eaten with a מום without פדיון, so their תמורה can be too. Regular קדשים need פדיון before they are eaten, so their תמורה also needs פדיון. This תמורה's holiness is too weak to be redeemed, so the path to eating it is closed and it must die.

keyTerms.meaning: It carries its 'mother's' name, meaning the identity of the animal it replaced
An animal that was swapped for a קרבן
Redeeming a holy animal by moving its holiness onto money
Is not strong enough
To take hold, to pass onto

steps.whatToRemember: A תמורה follows the animal it replaced. Since the replaced animal could be eaten only after פדיון, and this תמורה cannot be redeemed, it can never be eaten.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Its mother' does not mean the animal that gave birth to it. It means the original קרבן that this תמורה was swapped for.

phrases.english: And this one carries its mother's name,
phrases.notes: 'Mother' here means the original animal it replaced.

phrases.english: it is called 'the substitute of sacrificial animals',

phrases.aramaic: מָה קָדָשִׁים לָא מִיתַּכְלִי אֶלָּא בְּפִדְיוֹן —
phrases.english: just as sacrificial animals are eaten only through redemption —
so too their substitutes also
are eaten only through redemption,
and this one is not strong enough for its redemption to take hold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer from Step 16 by applying it to our case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on the identity of the replaced animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב עמרם thought every תמורה with a מום could be eaten, like the תמורה of בכור or מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: A תמורה follows its original animal. This one needs פדיון, cannot get it, and therefore must die.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן with a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks where we learn that the תמורה of פסולי המוקדשין must die. It answers from the פסוק 'ממעלי הגרה... טמא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב נחמן: From where do we know that the תמורה of disqualified holy animals must die? The פסוק says: 'Of those that chew the cud... it is impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב נחמן's ruling and gives it a source in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12-17 explained the ruling through logic about פדיון. Now the ruling also gets a פסוק. The extra word 'טמא' hints that some animal has kosher signs and is still forbidden to eat, and the ברייתא says this means our תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
Holy animals that became unfit, usually through a מום
From where do we learn this?
The פסוק teaches
From those that chew the cud

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ruling is not just reasoning. It also has support in the תורה.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Nachman:
From where do we know regarding the substitute of disqualified consecrated animals
that it must die?
The verse states: 'Of those that chew the cud... impure',
phrases.notes: ויקרא י״א:ד. The word 'impure' is read as a hint to an animal with kosher signs that is still forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logic is settled, the גמרא adds a ברייתא that gives the ruling a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that the תמורה of פסולי המוקדשין must die
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ממעלי הגרה... טמא (ויקרא י״א:ד)

steps.title: Isn't that פסוק needed for the five חטאות מתות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the same word 'טמא' is needed to teach about the five חטאות מתות, so it may not be free to teach about our תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is needed for the five חטאות that are left to die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's source. It suggests the פסוק is already being used for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק that is 'used up' for one law usually cannot also teach a second law. If 'טמא' is needed for the five חטאות מתות, the ברייתא's proof for our תמורה falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for something else
Five kinds of חטאת animals that cannot be offered or eaten and are left to die

phrases.english: But this is needed
for the five sin offerings that are left to die!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְחָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא's use of the פסוק from Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of ממעלי הגרה... טמא for the תמורה of פסולי המוקדשין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already taken for the five חטאות מתות, so it cannot also teach about our תמורה.

steps.title: The five חטאות מתות come from a different phrase
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the five חטאות מתות are learned from the parallel phrase 'ממפריסי הפרסה טמא', so 'ממעלי הגרה' is free for our תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one is learned from 'Of those that have a split hoof... impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ברייתא by pointing to a second phrase in the same פסוק that covers the five חטאות מתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two parallel phrases: 'chew the cud' and 'split hoof'. Each one teaches a different case. The 'split hoof' phrase covers the five חטאות מתות, so the 'chew the cud' phrase stays free for our תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Those with a split hoof
It is derived from

phrases.english: That one is from 'Of those that have a split hoof... impure'
it is derived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each law its own phrase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One word 'טמא' had to cover both the five חטאות מתות and our תמורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two separate phrases teach two separate laws.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the 'split hoof' source
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא agrees: the five חטאות מתות are learned from 'ממפריסי הפרסה... טמא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: From where do we know about the five חטאות that are left to die? The פסוק says: 'Of those that have a split hoof... impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up its answer from Step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the answer in Step 20 is not just a guess. A ברייתא really does link the five חטאות מתות to the 'split hoof' phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way, introducing a supporting ברייתא

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
From where do we know about the five sin offerings that are left to die?
The verse states: 'Of those that have a split hoof... impure.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 20 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the five חטאות מתות come from ממפריסי הפרסה... טמא

steps.title: The five חטאות מתות are a הלכה, not from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the five חטאות מתות are a הלכה למשה מסיני, so they do not need a פסוק at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The five חטאות that are left to die are a הלכה that we learned by tradition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the second ברייתא. Why would it need a פסוק for something we already know by tradition?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the law comes from a tradition handed down from סיני, a פסוק is not needed to teach it. So the 'split hoof' phrase must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: A הלכה למשה מסיני, a law passed down by tradition
We learned it by tradition

phrases.english: The five sin offerings that are left to die
are a law we learned by tradition!

steps.triggerLanguage: חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת הִילְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא brought in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that uses ממפריסי הפרסה for the five חטאות מתות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law known as a הלכה למשה מסיני does not need a פסוק.

steps.title: The פסוק really teaches תמורת אשם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'split hoof' phrase actually teaches the law of תמורת אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when the פסוק came, it came to teach about the תמורה of an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes what the 'split hoof' phrase teaches: not the five חטאות מתות, but תמורת אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the five חטאות מתות are already known by tradition, the פסוק must teach a new case. The new case is the תמורה of an אשם, which cannot be offered and is left to graze until it gets a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: When the פסוק came, meaning what it is really teaching
An animal swapped for an אשם

phrases.english: Rather, when the verse came,
it came for the substitute of a guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי אֲתָא קְרָא לִתְמוּרַת אָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 22 by moving the פסוק to a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the פסוק to a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'split hoof' phrase teaches the five חטאות מתות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'split hoof' phrase teaches תמורת אשם.

steps.title: תמורת אשם is also a known הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again: תמורת אשם is also known by tradition, under the rule that whatever dies in a חטאת grazes in an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תמורה of an אשם is also a הלכה! Whatever case dies with a חטאת is left to graze with an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 23 and knocks it down. The next step answers by returning to the five חטאות מתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule: in any case where a חטאת is left to die, an אשם in the same case is left to graze. Since a חטאת's תמורה dies, an אשם's תמורה must graze, and we know this without a פסוק. So the 'split hoof' phrase once again seems to have nothing to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: Any case where a חטאת is left to die
In an אשם, it is left to graze until it gets a מום

steps.confusionAlert: 'Grazing' does not mean the animal is free to use. It means it is left in the field until it gets a מום, and then it is redeemed.

phrases.english: The substitute of a guilt offering is also a traditional law,
whatever is left to die in the case of a sin offering —
in the case of a guilt offering is left to graze!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ממפריסי הפרסה teaches תמורת אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תמורת אשם is already known through the tradition that whatever dies in a חטאת grazes in an אשם, so no פסוק is needed.

steps.title: Both the verse and the tradition are needed for the five sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to saying the verse is about the five חטאות מתות. Both the פסוק and the הלכה are needed. The הלכה teaches that the animals are left to die. The פסוק teaches that eating them breaks a full לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse really is about the five sin offerings that are left to die. Both a verse and a tradition are needed. If we had only the verse, I would think the animals are left to graze. So the tradition teaches that they are left to die. If we had only the tradition, I would think that someone who happened to eat from these five sin offerings broke only a general prohibition, not a לאו. So the verse teaches that there is a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 22 by explaining that the verse and the tradition each teach a different detail about the five חטאות מתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that if the law is a הלכה למשה מסיני, a verse is not needed. The answer splits the job in two. The הלכה tells us what to do with the animal (let it die, not graze). The פסוק, with the word 'טמא', turns eating it into a real לאו, so the punishment is more serious.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. It signals a return to an earlier position.
It is needed
The tradition, meaning a הלכה למשה מסיני
Grazing. The animal is left to pasture until it gets a blemish.
A general prohibition, which carries no lashes
A negative commandment from the תורה, which can carry lashes

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two pieces. The tradition teaches HOW the animal is handled (it dies). The verse teaches HOW SEVERE it is to eat it (a full לאו). Neither one alone gives the whole picture.

phrases.english: Rather, really it is about the five sin offerings left to die,
phrases.notes: This returns to the answer given in step 20.

phrases.english: and the verse is needed and the tradition is needed,
for if it were only from the verse, I would have said they go to graze,
so the tradition teaches us that they are left to die.
And if it were only from the tradition, I would have said:
where someone happened to
eat from these five sin offerings,
there is a prohibition, but there is no לאו,
so the verse teaches us that there is a לאו.
phrases.notes: The word 'טמא' in the verse creates the לאו.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת, וְאִצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא וְאִצְטְרִיךְ הִילְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 24 knocked out the תמורת אשם answer. The גמרא now returns to the step 20 answer and defends it against the step 22 challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that both sources are needed because each teaches something different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the verse, the animals would graze. With only the tradition, eating them would be a general prohibition with no לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tradition teaches that the animals die. The verse makes eating them a full לאו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic pattern. A פסוק and a הלכה למשה מסיני can exist side by side when each adds a separate detail. Here the details are how the animal is handled and how severe the punishment is.

steps.title: The verse compares our substitute animal to the five sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the five חטאות מתות are known from tradition alone. The verse is a היקש. Its purpose is to compare the law learned from 'מעלי גרה' (our תמורה) to the law learned from 'מפריסי הפרסה' (the five חטאות). Just as those die, our תמורה dies too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: the verse comes to compare the law that comes from 'those who chew the cud' to the law that comes from 'those who have a split hoof'. Just as there the animals are left to die, so too here they are left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer. The verse is not the source for the five חטאות at all. It is a comparison that tells us how our תמורה is treated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer, the five חטאות מתות come purely from tradition, so the challenge from step 22 does not apply. The verse places 'מעלי גרה' (our תמורה) and 'מפריסי הפרסה' (the five חטאות) side by side. That teaches that our תמורה is also left to die, not to graze.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say. This introduces a second, alternate answer.
To compare by היקש, meaning two things placed together in one verse
Those who chew the cud. Here it hints at our תמורה.
Those with a split hoof. Here it hints at the five חטאות.
There, meaning the other case

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers end this section. (1) The verse and the tradition are both needed for the five חטאות: one teaches death, the other teaches the לאו. (2) The verse is a היקש that makes our תמורה die just like the five חטאות.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: it is to compare
a matter that comes from 'those who chew the cud'
to a matter that comes from 'those who have a split hoof',
phrases.notes: These are the five חטאות מתות.

phrases.english: just as there it is left to die,
so too here it is left to die.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְאַקּוֹשֵׁי דָּבָר הַבָּא מִמַּעֲלֵי גֵּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It offers a second way out of the step 22 challenge, instead of the צריכותא in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the verse to a היקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think our תמורה is left to graze.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the היקש to the five חטאות, our תמורה is left to die.

steps.title: New משנה: taking animals from a gentile in a guaranteed deal
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. Its case is a Jew who receives animals from a gentile under a צאן ברזל arrangement.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who receives 'iron sheep' (a guaranteed investment) from a gentile...
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It is setting up a case, and the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In צאן ברזל, the Jew raises the gentile's animals and guarantees their fixed value even if they die. The offspring are shared. This sets up the question of whether the offspring are obligated in בכורה, since partial ownership by a gentile matters for that law.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה.
One who receives
'Iron sheep': a deal where the value is guaranteed like iron, which never gets used up
A non-Jew

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who receives 'iron sheep' from a gentile,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמְקַבֵּל צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִן הַגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new topic. The previous sugya about תמורה has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is introduced here. The ruling about the offspring follows on the next amud.
